open_questions.q: When every child of an inline child table is unchanged (and --show-unchanged-values is not set), should the table be omitted silently or replaced by a one-line note?
open_questions.assumed: Keep the child section heading and replace the table with a one-line italic note (e.g. '_No route changes._'), matching the existing '_No attribute changes._' note for attribute tables.

open_questions.q: Should a child table note how many unchanged children were hidden (e.g. '_8 unchanged routes hidden._')?
open_questions.assumed: No. Attribute tables hide unchanged rows without a count; --show-unchanged-values is the documented way to see them.

open_questions.q: docs/features.md says unchanged NSG security rules are shown with ⏺️ 'for completeness', and NSG security rules are a parent-child pattern. Does this feature override that?
open_questions.assumed: Yes. All parent-child child tables, including NSG security rules, hide unchanged rows by default, as the reporter asks for uniform behaviour.

open_questions.q: Should provider-specific tables outside parent-child grouping that also show ⏺️ rows (firewall rule collections, build definition, variable group) follow the same rule?
open_questions.assumed: No, out of scope; they render as today. A follow-up can extend the rule.

open_questions.q: On a parent replace, should unchanged children still be hidden?
open_questions.assumed: Yes, matching attribute tables, which hide unchanged attributes on a replace too.
